rows.what_changes: cluster id "A" (scalar sum 65): fill, stroke and the label fill go from hsl(65, 55%, 60%) to hsl(0, 55%, 60%). Every cluster becomes hue 0, red
rows.reason: For hash>=0, (hash*360+360)%360 is always 0, so only the cluster colour string changes. An id whose original hue is already 0 (e.g. the empty string) is unchanged. The hue is an Int printed as digits, so the markup stays well-formed. hash*360 is a checked multiply and could trap only for hash > Int.max/360, which needs about 2.3e10 maximal scalars in one module name. That is not practically reachable, and a trap would be a crash, not malformed output.

rows.what_changes: cluster id "A" (65): the colour goes from hsl(65, 55%, 60%) to hsl(-295, 55%, 60%), the same angle mod 360, so it renders the same colour but the text differs
rows.reason: Swift's % truncates, so ((hash%360)-360)%360 equals (hash%360)-360 for a nonzero remainder (a hue in -359...-1), and 0 when the remainder is 0. Only the hue number inside the colour string changes. A leading '-' is legal in an attribute value, and there are no references.

rows.what_changes: cluster id "A" (65): the colour goes from hsl(65, 55%, 60%) to hsl(153000, 55%, 60%), which is 0 mod 360, so every cluster renders red
rows.reason: (r+360)*360 with r in 0...359 is a multiple of 360 between 129600 and 258840. It cannot overflow, and its only effect is the hue text in the fill, stroke and label fill colour strings. It prints as plain digits, so the XML stays well-formed. No ids or references are touched.

Both branches emit well-formed markup and a url(#markerId) that resolves.

The law generator never produces it either (columns 0/100/200). The public renderFromLayout accepts any SequenceMessage, though, so a gap of 1 is an accepted input and flips line to path. Both branches are well formed and reference a defined marker.
